insights.title: Downpours are becoming more common
insights.body: Days with 20 mm or more of rain went from about 21 to 27 a year (first vs last 10 years). Bare soil during these storms washes away fastest.

insights.body: Yearly rain went from about 2535 mm to 2722 mm.

outlook.method: Theil-Sen trend + Mann-Kendall test on 2001-2024 yearly data, extended to 2035 with an 80% prediction range. Where there is no clear trend, the 2001-2024 average is projected. Statistical extrapolation, not a climate-model forecast.

consequences.headline: More downpours: about 33 heavy-rain days a year by 2035
consequences.detail: Up from about 24 today. Each downpour on bare soil washes away topsoil and the fertiliser in it; fields here are barest in Feb, Jul and Aug.
consequences.action: Keep the ground covered (a legume or crop residue) through the rainy months.

consequences.headline: Pigeon pea fits 3 points worse by 2035
consequences.detail: If today's trends continue: Pigeon pea 55 → 52 (crop match out of 100).
consequences.action: Build the rotation around crops whose match holds up.

consequences.headline: +0.6 °C warmer on average by 2035
consequences.detail: The yearly average moves from 27.1 °C to about 27.7 °C. Most recommended crops stay inside their temperature range.
consequences.action: Watch heat stress in cool-climate crops; earlier sowing helps.

consequences.headline: About 12% more rain by 2035
consequences.detail: Yearly rain trends from about 2,616 mm to 2,928 mm. More water, but also more waterlogging on heavy soil.
consequences.action: Keep drains open; raised beds help crops that hate wet feet.
